deckTitle: Politics — The Starter Set of Doom: 5,000 Years of Bad Ideas & One Very Tired Ballot Box
verdict: This is the political theory syllabus as carnival barker manifesto — Caesar, Machiavelli, The Permanent Secretary, The Narrative Manager are all murder-lineup archetypes that snap into performance the moment a player reads them. The tactic/weapon/promo card-type system creates genuine mechanical depth: you're not just playing characters, you're playing moves, weapons, and gambits in distinct registers. Named strength: the sheer density of instantly playable lore lines — 'Ministers come and go. We remain.' is a full character in four words. Named weakness: the four Promo cards are orphans — they reference The Demagogue, The Donor, The Lobbyist, and The Bureaucrat, none of which appear in this deck, leaving Promos unresolvable without a companion set. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 52 cards of political archetypes, tactics, and weapons — from Machiavelli to the Narrative Manager. For anyone who ever watched a press conference and thought 'I could run this kayfabe better.'

coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'Starter Set of Doom: 5,000 Years of Bad Ideas & One Very Tired Ballot Box' is a knockout retail hook
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — cover IS the deck: political kayfabe chaos rendered in one image with perfect tonal precision
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — starburst badges ('Now with 30% More Technocracy!', '$18.99 → YOUR SOUL', 'Ages 18-Death') are genre-inventing
coverQA.coverViral: 5 — every badge is a shareable standalone; the fine print page closes the loop with full brand commitment
coverQA.coverNote: That cover does in one image what most decks need three pages to attempt — FrizzleBob holding a VOTES box, a $ bag, and a lit stick of dynamite is the entire political spectrum compressed into one rabbit. The dead-cat badge and soul-price tag are screenshot-ready before anyone reads a single card. This is the strongest cover in the corpus so far.

notes: Two distinct card formats co-exist: character cards (pages 2-4) display RAF stats [R:X][A:X][F:X] and use italic lore without a 'Lore:' label; tactic/weapon/promo/event cards (pages 5-14) use bracket type tags ([Instant Action], [Attack], etc.) and explicit 'Lore:' / 'Power:' labels — no RAF stats. This split is intentional and readable but RAF-only players may find the tactic cards feel like a different game. The four Promo cards (page 14) reference four absent archetypes (The Demagogue, The Donor, The Lobbyist, The Bureaucrat, plus Narcissist card and Parliament deck) — cross-deck dependencies needing companion set context or standalone rewrites. Fine Print page (p.15) is brilliant brand voice: 'Do not feed the politicians after midnight' and 'Void where prohibited by dictators!' are Gumroad-preview gold. The 'Dead Cat Expansion' badge on the cover corresponds to the Distraction Tactic card on page 6.

cards.power: Ostracism: Exile any player who becomes too powerful. The audience talks back.
cards.lore: Aristotle called us political animals. He meant it as a compliment. We have complicated the assessment.
cards.gradeReason: Strong historical frame, clear role — but needs table context to unlock full performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-wash watercolor. Subject: wise owl atop cracked Greek amphora. Mood: civic melancholy.

cards.power: The Worked Shoot: Violate the constitution publicly. Generals must disband armies; you kept yours.
cards.lore: The Republic survived the crossing. The political reality did not.
cards.gradeReason: Power IS the move — violate the constitution publicly and dare anyone to stop you. Table erupts.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dramatic watercolor. Subject: armored wolf-general wading river in full battle splatter. Mood: triumphant menace.

cards.power: The Prince: Perform virtue while doing the terrible thing. Do it all at once.
cards.lore: Everyone sees what you appear to be; few experience what you really are.
cards.gradeReason: Crystalline G1: perform virtue and do the terrible thing simultaneously — no interpretation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Renaissance watercolor. Subject: sly fox in doublet holding dagger and quill. Mood: silky danger.

cards.power: Realpolitik: The election is theater. You are the machinery.
cards.lore: Give them the performance of representation and they won't notice the absence of substance.
cards.gradeReason: Walrus-chancellor energy is readable; power needs a table primed on realpolitik to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: military portrait watercolor. Subject: walrus general in Prussian uniform smoking cigar. Mood: smug authority.

cards.power: The Rally: Convert every action into a performance. Reality checks require a BLÖDSINN! roll.
cards.lore: I alone can fix it. The institutions are the enemy. You are with me or you are with them.
cards.gradeReason: Lore IS the character — play it and every action becomes theater. Instant demagogue mode.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: agitprop watercolor. Subject: hyena on soapbox roaring into megaphone at crowd. Mood: manic energy.

cards.power: The Briefing: Establish expertise. Your next action cannot be challenged on facts, only on tone.
cards.lore: The data suggests your anger is statistically insignificant.
cards.gradeReason: Beaver-with-clipboard archetype is sharp; tone-only challenge mechanic requires setup to exploit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate watercolor. Subject: bespectacled beaver with calculator and clipboard. Mood: detached condescension.

cards.power: Institutional Memory: Reactivate a played card at half strength. You know where the bodies are buried.
cards.lore: I have served under seven Prime Ministers. I intend to serve under several more.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is G1-tier; power requires other cards on table and some game history to be electric.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: French court watercolor. Subject: cockroach in tuxedo raising champagne amid mushroom cloud. Mood: serene survivalism.

cards.power: Conviction: Your narrative cannot be redirected. You hold the line until you burn out.
cards.lore: This is worth doing even if it costs me everything. (Spoiler: It will).
cards.gradeReason: The spoiler in the lore does the work — player immediately knows to embody doomed righteousness.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: protest watercolor. Subject: earnest lamb marching with CHANGE NOW! sign. Mood: doomed conviction.

cards.power: The Network: Connect any two cards. Resolve a problem immediately without a roll.
cards.lore: I'm going to need you to make some calls. No, different calls.
cards.gradeReason: Spider-in-phone-web is vivid; connecting two cards for no-roll resolution needs game context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir watercolor. Subject: spider at center of web made from old mobile phones. Mood: covert control.

cards.power: The Line to Take: Pre-narrate the response to a disaster. +1 Defense against reality.
cards.lore: It's not a lie. It's a curated sequence of factual elements.
cards.gradeReason: Murder-tier lore line; '+1 Defense against reality' is instantly performable as spin doctor mode.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: urban watercolor. Subject: chameleon painting over overflowing trash cans on brick wall. Mood: cheerful deception.

cards.power: The Briefing Pack: Add a 'Consideration' to any action. Three Considerations make action impossible.
cards.lore: Ministers come and go. We remain.
cards.gradeReason: Four words, whole ideology. The Consideration mechanic is the bureaucratic soul made mechanical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bureaucratic watercolor. Subject: sloth stamping DENIED in towering paperwork avalanche. Mood: immovable sluggishness.

cards.power: The Invisible Hand: Amplify a card's effect. The access is invisible; the results are real.
cards.lore: I didn't buy the politician. I invested in a shared value system.
cards.gradeReason: Peak corrupt-donor energy: the lore is a ready-made character voice you step into at once.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: plutocrat watercolor. Subject: fat cat in pinstripe suit pouring champagne into ballot box. Mood: brazen corruption.

cards.power: The Mirror: You must begin every turn talking about yourself. If accepted, +1 Power.
cards.lore: It's not a disorder if it wins elections.
cards.gradeReason: Role is vivid but 'if accepted' gating requires table buy-in before the narcissism lands.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: peacock watercolor. Subject: preening peacock admiring mirror while backdrop burns. Mood: vain obliviousness.

cards.power: The Frame: Reframe a failure as a strategic necessity. Can only be blocked by checking Plausibility.
cards.lore: Have no fixed position. Have no genuine belief. Win.
cards.gradeReason: Three-word manifesto. The move — reframe failure as strategy — is immediately performable at any table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chess-noir watercolor. Subject: coiled snake moving chess pieces on board. Mood: cold calculation.

cards.power: No Brakes: Immune to emotional appeals. Can only be stopped by mechanics, not morals.
cards.lore: Stress immunity is a leadership asset. So is lack of empathy.
cards.gradeReason: Archetype is clear; mechanical immunity to morals needs table conflict context to generate real tension.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate noir watercolor. Subject: shark in business suit with predatory grin. Mood: icy detachment.

cards.power: Feedback Loop: Double the effect of any Narcissist card.
cards.lore: The audience believes the performance. The performer believes the audience.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is beautiful but power is dead without a 'Narcissist' card — references absent deck content.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: baroque watercolor. Subject: ornate gilded mirror reflecting crown in dark void. Mood: narcissistic infinity.

cards.power: Shock Value: Suspend the current losing narrative. Force everyone to address the Cat.
cards.lore: If you are losing the argument, throw a dead cat on the table. Now everyone is talking about the cat.
cards.gradeReason: The move is in the name — every player knows exactly what to do and how to perform it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dinner-party watercolor. Subject: dead cat placed on formal dining table amid horrified guests. Mood: chaotic absurdity.

cards.power: Split Vote: Break an alliance between two other cards. They must operate independently.
cards.lore: Make them choose between their values and their friends.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is a knife but the alliance-breaking mechanic requires existing table alliances to be meaningful.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: action watercolor. Subject: beaver splitting stone heart with sledgehammer. Mood: brutal precision.

cards.power: Deniability: Play face down. Reveal information later. The source is never identified.
cards.lore: Trial balloon? Hostile disclosure? It's not gossip if it's anonymous.
cards.gradeReason: Face-down mechanic is satisfying; needs a table sophisticated enough to enjoy the slow reveal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: spy watercolor. Subject: trench-coat rat at backstage microphone in curtained alcove. Mood: shadowy deniability.

cards.power: Redirection: Reduce the effect of a negative card by 50% and change the topic.
cards.lore: I'm glad you asked that question, because the real issue is…
cards.gradeReason: Classic political dodge — recognizable but the 50% reduction needs a clearer in-play signal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: action watercolor. Subject: weasel in tuxedo hurling grenade and vanishing in POOF cloud. Mood: slippery escape.

cards.power: Technicality: Negate an accusation based on wording, not substance.
cards.lore: I did not do *that* specific thing, in *that* specific way.
cards.gradeReason: The asterisk emphasis in lore IS the performance — any player reads it and knows exactly how to deliver.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: legal watercolor. Subject: squid spraying black NO-smoke above court documents and gavel. Mood: technical obstruction.

cards.power: Fill Time: Consume an opponent's turn without giving them anything to attack.
cards.lore: Let me be very clear about my position (without stating the position).
cards.gradeReason: Politician-parrot is instantly funny; filling time without substance needs confident improv to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political watercolor. Subject: parrot in suit at podium with bridge behind. Mood: verbose vacuity.

cards.power: Escape: Bypass a restriction or rule for one turn.
cards.lore: It follows the letter of the law while violating its spirit entirely.
cards.gradeReason: Worm-in-apple-labyrinth is evocative; bypass mechanic is useful but doesn't demand a performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surreal watercolor. Subject: bureaucratic worm navigating labyrinthine tunnels inside red apple. Mood: systemic absurdity.

cards.power: Suspension: Remove the 'Parliament' deck from play for one round.
cards.lore: If the legislature is annoying you, send them home.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is gloriously blunt; Suspension requires a Parliament deck that may not be in play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: institutional watercolor. Subject: turtle in hard hat locking parliament doors with heavy chains. Mood: smug authoritarianism.

cards.power: Authenticity: Connect with the "common voter." Immune to BLÖDSINN! checks this turn.
cards.lore: Kiss the baby. Ignore the diaper. Smile for the camera.
cards.gradeReason: Three-beat lore sequence IS the scene — player picks up the baby and performance writes itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: campaign watercolor. Subject: wolf politician grinning, holding crying piglet for camera flashes. Mood: performed warmth.

cards.power: Momentum: If you keep moving, they can't ask questions.
cards.lore: Spontaneity is organized. The organization is invisible.
cards.gradeReason: Bus-over-cliff image is perfect; Momentum's 'keep moving' power needs active narration to maintain.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: campaign trail watercolor. Subject: VOTE-painted bus racing full speed toward cliff edge. Mood: reckless momentum.

cards.power: Soundbite: Win the round by being Persuasive, not Accurate.
cards.lore: It's not about policy. It's about who sighs louder.
cards.gradeReason: Flaming podium tells the whole story — play it and immediately start performing Persuasive over Accurate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: debate watercolor. Subject: flaming podium on empty stage, timer frozen at 00:00. Mood: theatrical disaster.

cards.power: Turnout: Add +1 to any die roll through sheer volume of labor.
cards.lore: Twitter isn't real life. This is real life.
cards.gradeReason: Ant-army image is wonderful; +1 via labor is mechanically clean but low drama as a performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: grassroots watercolor. Subject: army of ants knocking on tree-stump door with clipboards. Mood: determined groundswell.

cards.power: Obstruction: No cards can be played while the Filibuster is active.
cards.lore: I will read this recipe for pot liquor until you give up.
cards.gradeReason: Filibuster turtle reading pot liquor recipes — the role is perfectly embodied before a word is spoken.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: parliamentary watercolor. Subject: turtle at podium reading recipe book to cobwebbed senators. Mood: weaponized boredom.

cards.power: Vote: Force a majority vote. If lost, the current Leader is suspended.
cards.lore: We do not believe this government should continue.
cards.gradeReason: Power is dramatic; forcing a vote is table-dependent — only generates fire when a Leader is established.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gothic watercolor. Subject: hooded figure toppling throne into swirling dark water. Mood: cold constitutional violence.

cards.power: Disruption: Cancel an opponent's action by demanding a headcount.
cards.lore: Stop what you are doing and prove you exist.
cards.gradeReason: Chirping cricket in parliament is brilliant — headcount disruption mechanic is satisfying procedural chaos.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: procedural watercolor. Subject: cricket chirping at podium in vast empty parliamentary chamber. Mood: bureaucratic absurdity.

cards.power: Overload: Bury an action in so much process it essentially dies.
cards.lore: We have a few thousand minor suggestions.
cards.gradeReason: Paper-tidal-wave image is visceral; 'essentially dies' could use sharper table-resolution language.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bureaucratic watercolor. Subject: humans fleeing tidal wave of government memos and forms. Mood: overwhelmed futility.

cards.power: Forced Position: No neutrality allowed. You must declare a side or lose power.
cards.lore: Never let a good crisis go to waste. Who benefits?
cards.gradeReason: Dumpster-fire-marshmallow image is iconic; Forced Position is powerful but context-dependent.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: crisis watercolor. Subject: suited politicians roasting marshmallows over flaming dumpster. Mood: gleeful opportunism.

cards.power: Freeze: All cards on stage are frozen until a "Finding" is narrated.
cards.lore: We will report in 18 months. By then, everyone will have forgotten.
cards.gradeReason: Magnifying glass over empty room is perfect; Freeze needs a clear end-trigger to avoid stalling.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: investigative watercolor. Subject: enormous magnifying glass examining empty white room. Mood: performative inquiry.

cards.power: Joint Custody: Two players must narrate every move together. If they disagree, it fails.
cards.lore: We agree on nothing. We are governing together.
cards.gradeReason: Coalition-partners-as-hissing-animals is G1-tier art; joint narration mechanic requires coordination.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: coalition watercolor. Subject: cat and dog tied at tail by rope, both furious. Mood: miserable co-dependency.

cards.power: Silence: The affected player cannot speak directly; they must use a 'Spokesperson'.
cards.lore: The scandal isn't what they did. It's the hypocrisy.
cards.gradeReason: Skeleton-in-wardrobe is perfect. Spokesperson requirement is fun improv but needs a willing player pair.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: scandal watercolor. Subject: skeleton falling from ornate cobwebbed wardrobe. Mood: long-delayed exposure.

cards.power: Resolution: Resolve all pending provocations. No more spin.
cards.lore: The numbers come in. The meaning is different for everyone.
cards.gradeReason: Roller-coaster-crash is evocative; Resolution is the rare clean-up card that needs pending chaos to matter.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: election-night watercolor. Subject: roller coaster crashing off track, riders screaming. Mood: chaotic accountability.

cards.power: Stabilize: If performed graciously, the game stabilizes. If refused, chaos ensues.
cards.lore: The loser must say the system works. Otherwise, it doesn't.
cards.gradeReason: Handkerchief wave is ritually resonant; gracious performance gate is a genuine improv test for the player.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ritual watercolor. Subject: gloved formal hand holding white handkerchief. Mood: dignified surrender.

cards.power: Second Act: Re-enter the game with a sympathy bonus.
cards.lore: You won't have Nixon to kick around anymore. (Wait, he's back).
cards.gradeReason: Nixon parenthetical is the whole move — you get eliminated, come back, the table already has the joke.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: zombie-resurrection watercolor. Subject: suited zombie rising from 1998-dated gravestone. Mood: inevitable comeback.

cards.power: Truce: Suspend all Monster cards for one round.
cards.lore: The hands are real. What happens next is just not written yet.
cards.gradeReason: Reptile-human handshake is arresting; Truce is strong but Monster card dependency needs flagging.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: diplomatic watercolor. Subject: reptilian and human hands shaking amid olive branches. Mood: cautious fragile optimism.

cards.power: Recontextualize: Force an opponent to accept a negative interpretation of their past moves.
cards.lore: I'm just sharing information. The information speaks for itself.
cards.gradeReason: Cockroach-with-folder is instantly playable — say that lore line and you are already in character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: spy-noir watercolor. Subject: cockroach operative clutching folder of incriminating photographs. Mood: deniable threat.

cards.power: Truth Bomb: Sacrifice your position to shift the narrative 3 steps toward Truth.
cards.lore: I have said the thing. Now you have to live with it.
cards.gradeReason: Feedback-screech on empty stage is inspired; sacrificing your position requires genuine player commitment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sacrifice watercolor. Subject: microphone producing lightning feedback on dramatically lit empty stage. Mood: costly honesty.

cards.power: Auto-Resolve: Fix one problem instantly. No questions asked.
cards.lore: It's already done. I made some calls.
cards.gradeReason: Shadowed-hand-in-archway is evocative; instant fix is a strong play but low in performative invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: backroom watercolor. Subject: shadowed hand passing gold coins through dark stone archway. Mood: transactional power.

cards.power: Pre-Narration: Define the reality before it happens.
cards.lore: Stick to the grid. Don't answer the question asked.
cards.gradeReason: Sweating pig with rolled-up script is great; Pre-Narration is G1-tier concept but naming is too abstract.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: media watercolor. Subject: sweating pig receiving rolled script from spotlit director hand. Mood: manufactured reality.

cards.power: Belief: If the table believes the lie, it becomes the rule.
cards.lore: The performance of power is the source of power.
cards.gradeReason: This card IS kayfabe theory — lore and power both demand you perform and commit fully. No instruction needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestler-suit watercolor. Subject: politician in patriotic luchador mask adjusting tie. Mood: performed legitimacy.

cards.power: Realness: Break the game rules to say something true. High risk.
cards.lore: The moment the mask slips. Dangerous. Valuable.
cards.gradeReason: Breaking game rules to say something true is the rarest G1 — it invites a genuine mask-off moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chaos watercolor. Subject: bear paws shredding government briefing documents mid-table. Mood: dangerous authenticity.

cards.power: Perspective: Change the victory conditions of the current scene.
cards.lore: Politics is a game. Don't hate the player, hate the dev team.
cards.gradeReason: FrizzleBob-rabbit-in-a-frame is meta-perfect; victory condition change is sophisticated but needs game state.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: meta watercolor. Subject: cartoon rabbit drawing frame around itself with pencil. Mood: self-aware irony.

cards.power: Civilization: Reset the chaos. We agree to this so we don't kill each other.
cards.lore: The curtain is thin. The curtain is the point.
cards.gradeReason: Power text is the best social contract definition on any card — you play it and the table goes quiet.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: democratic watercolor. Subject: feet of multiple voters visible under voting booth curtains. Mood: thin sacred civic weight.

cards.power: Connection: Works exactly like the Demagogue.
cards.lore: You people make me sick! (Cheer for me).
cards.gradeReason: Lore line is G1; power is dead — references The Demagogue, which is not in this deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling watercolor. Subject: bull wrestler screaming into vintage microphone. Mood: theatrical rage.

cards.power: Connection: Synergizes with The Donor.
cards.lore: The market decided. (I am the market).
cards.gradeReason: Lore is sharp; power references The Donor — absent from this deck, making Market unresolvable alone.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: divine watercolor. Subject: ghostly hand moving chess pieces amid falling currency. Mood: invisible authority.

cards.power: Connection: The Lobbyist's true form.
cards.lore: You invited me in. Now we discuss terms.
cards.gradeReason: Great lore and bat image; power text is a pure cross-deck reference with zero standalone playability.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vampire watercolor. Subject: upside-down bat in tuxedo dripping ink into jar. Mood: entitled extraction.

cards.power: Connection: The Bureaucrat's ultimate defense.
cards.lore: Let's circle back to that. Forever.
cards.gradeReason: Best lore of the four Promos; power is still a dead-end reference without The Bureaucrat at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hamster wheel watercolor. Subject: frantic hamster running wheel going nowhere fast. Mood: institutionalized inertia.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: POLITICS – The Starter Set of Doom: 5,000 Years of Bad Ideas & One Very Tired Ballot Box (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Politics is the oldest worked match on earth, and you have been buying ringside tickets your whole life.

Watch a real one work. A minister is losing the argument on live television, the numbers are bad, the question is fair, and an honest answer would end him. So he throws a dead cat on the table. Now nobody is discussing the numbers. Everyone is discussing the cat. That is not a gaffe, it is a named move with five thousand years of patch notes, and the same playbook runs from The Caesar wading back across the river with the army he was ordered to disband, to the Permanent Secretary who outlasts every minister by burying each decision under one more Consideration.

This is Social Story Wrestling pointed straight at power. 52 cut-and-play cards turn the whole apparatus into a match you can run at your own kitchen table: you pick up an archetype or a tactic, perform the move dead-straight like you mean it, and the room rules on whether the con holds or collapses the second someone names it out loud.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Politics Core Deck: 52 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Populist, The Permanent Secretary, and The Narrative Manager.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, no civics degree, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the one law that every card can claim anything, as long as you sell the pitch before the table calls a BLÖDSINN! roll on it.
- The Two-Tier Playbook: the deck runs the people who hold power and the moves they hold it with. Character archetypes carry their own stats, Caesar's Worked Shoot, Bismarck's Realpolitik, the Populist's Rally, and they sit alongside the dirty tricks they run, the Dead Cat distraction, the Filibuster that freezes the table until you give up, and the Lawyer's Edit that beats an accusation on wording instead of substance. You are not just playing who governs, you are playing how they keep it.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
Grab this deck and you are not buying a frozen PDF. You are joining the Komik Kard Kult cycle. Every future expansion in this series, every fresh roster of archetypes and dirty tricks, lands in your library as a free update. No second checkout, no committee to approve it.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I make these because a move you can name is a move that stops working on you. Once you have cut a promo as The Narrative Manager at your own table, telling the room with a straight face that it was never a lie, only a curated sequence of factual elements, you catch the real one the next time it walks out to a podium. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Cut it, play it, run the next press conference straight back at itself. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes directly into the time I spend drawing the next cards and sharpening the mechanics. Free to print, share and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
They have run this same match for five thousand years because the audience keeps clapping on cue. Learn the holds, and stop taking the bumps for free.
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
